issues.description: The problem statement and the template require Developer.attend(course:) to accept an optional Course? and instruct students to use optional binding. However, the reference solution implements attend(course:) with a non-optional parameter (Course). This divergence in the method signature contradicts the specification and the template guidance and may confuse students comparing their implementation with the solution or when following the optional-binding instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution consistent with the problem statement and template by changing the solution's attend method signature to accept an optional Course? (func attend(course: Course?)) and using optional binding inside the method as described in the problem. Alternatively, if the intended design is to require a non-optional Course, update the problem statement and template to specify a non-optional parameter and remove the optional-binding requirement.

issues.description: The attend(course:) method parameter is defined as an optional Course? in the Problem Statement and the TEMPLATE implementation, but the SOLUTION implementation uses a non-optional Course parameter. This mismatch in the method signature (optional vs non-optional) creates a semantic inconsistency: students are instructed to perform optional binding on an optional Course, but the reference solution accepts a non-optional Course. This can confuse learners about the expected parameter type and whether they must handle nil values when implementing attend(course:).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across all artifacts. Either make the solution accept an optional Course? and perform optional binding (preferred to match the problem instructions and template), or update the problem statement and template to require a non-optional Course and remove optional-binding instructions. Example fix: change the solution's signature to func attend(course: Course?) and use optional binding inside the method.
